[[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]] | after_party = No overall control }} The '''2024 Oxford City Council election''' was held on Thursday 2 May 2024, alongside the [[2024 UK local elections|other local elections being held in the United Kingdom]] on the same day.{{Cite web |title=Next Election for Oxford City Council |url=https://www.oxford.gov.uk/info/20046/elections_and_voting |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240107125333/https://www.oxford.gov.uk/info/20046/elections_and_voting |archive-date=7 Jan 2024 |access-date=7 Jan 2024 |website=Oxford City Council - oxford.gov.uk}} The councillors elected will serve a four-year term ending in 2028.{{Cite web |title=Composition of Oxford City Council |url=http://opencouncildata.co.uk/council.php?c=179&y=0 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240107125635/http://opencouncildata.co.uk/council.php?c=179&y=0 |archive-date=7 Jan 2024 |access-date=7 Jan 2024 |website=Open Council Data UK - opencouncildata.co.uk}} == Background == [[Oxford City Council]] elects half of its councillors to every 2 years to serve four-year terms. However, the seats up for election in 2024 were last [[2021 United Kingdom local elections|elected in 2021]], due to [[COVID-19 pandemic|the COVID-19 pandemic.]] At the [[2022 United Kingdom local elections|previous election in 2022]], [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]] held its majority on the council, however, they lost 3 seats to bring the total number of Labour councillors to 32.{{Cite news |title=Oxford result - Local Elections 2022 |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/election/2022/england/councils/E07000178 |access-date=2024-01-07 |work=BBC News |language=en-GB}}{{Cite web |last=Council |first=Oxford City |title=Oxford City Council Election results - 5 May 2022 |url=https://www.oxford.gov.uk/info/20046/elections_and_voting/1521/oxford_city_council_election_results_-_5_may_2022 |access-date=2024-01-07 |website=www.oxford.gov.uk |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2022-05-06 |title=Full breakdown of Oxford City Council local election results 2022 |url=https://www.oxfordmail.co.uk/news/20120902.oxford-city-council-local-election-results-may-2022---full-breakdown/ |access-date=2024-01-07 |website=Oxford Mail |language=en}} In October 2023, Labour lost control of the council due to 9 councillors resigning in opposition to [[Sir Keir Starmer|Keir Starmer's]] refusal to call for a ceasefire in the [[Gaza war]].{{Cite web |title=Labour Loses Oxford City Council Over Gaza |url=https://tribunemag.co.uk/2023/10/labour-just-lost-control-of-oxford-city-council-over-starmers-comments-on-gaza |access-date=2024-01-07 |website=tribunemag.co.uk |language=en-GB}} By the time of the election the council remained under [[no overall control]], with a Labour leader.{{Cite news |date=2023-10-26 |title=Labour loses Oxford council majority after ninth Gaza resignation |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-oxfordshire-67231473 |access-date=2024-01-07 |work=BBC News |language=en-GB}} [[Robert Ford (academic)|Robert Ford]] suggested in ''[[The Guardian]]'' that Oxford would be a key testing ground of dissatisfaction from Labour's left wing and from Muslim and young progressive voters.{{cite web |author1=Robert Ford |author1-link=Robert Ford (academic) |title=Red walls and green dreams: what are the key battlegrounds in England’s local elections? |url=https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2024/apr/28/england-local-elections-2-may-polls-westminster-race |website=[[The Guardian]] |access-date=28 April 2024 |date=28 April 2024}} ==Summary== [[File:Svgfiles 2024-05-27-14-08-07-050501-caeeba2e7b4f4fc6f8ad058134e591720f147d8c8de371db7c2334b33c07a933.svg|left|thumb|Oxford City Council's composition following the 2024 election.]] Following the election, the council remained under no overall control. Labour made a net loss of a further two seats, but remained the largest party on the council. They continued to run the council as a minority administration after the election.{{cite news |last1=Manuschka |first1=Jacob |title=Oxford City Council announces new cabinet and sets out aims |url=https://www.oxfordmail.co.uk/news/24327281.oxford-city-council-announces-new-cabinet-sets-aims/ |access-date=15 July 2024 |work=Oxford Mail |date=18 May 2024}} The Green Party gained two seats. There was a net loss of four independent councillors. A new local party, the Independent Oxford Alliance (IOA), which had only been created earlier in 2024, won four seats.{{cite news |last1=Qurashi |first1=Noor |title=Oxford Independent Alliance candidates share pledges |url=https://www.oxfordmail.co.uk/news/24125881.oxford-independent-alliance-candidates-share-pledges/ |access-date=15 July 2024 |work=Oxford Mail |date=17 February 2024}}
